review_evidence: Original Zidd-authored English content; NCERT structural alignment reviewed against the source map
title: The Rainbow
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: See the bridge in the sky
levels.focus: understand the rainbow image and its central comparison
levels.teaching_goal: Explain how details about shape, colour, and position make a rainbow resemble a bridge between earth and sky.

guided_check.teaching_block: A poetic image helps a reader picture an idea. A high curved band can resemble a bridge even though nobody can walk across it.
guided_check.passage: When the shower ended, a bright arc curved above the mango trees and seemed to reach from one side of the field to the other.
guided_check.prompt: Which image best matches the bright arc?

bridge.teaching_block: To understand a comparison, name the feature both things share. An arched gate and a rainbow both make a curve above an open space.
bridge.passage: Kabir looked through a curved garden gate. Beyond it, a band of colours made a second curve in the distance.
bridge.prompt: What shared feature makes the gate and the band of colours look alike?
options: both can be opened by hand
both stand on the garden path

masterclass.teaching_block: A main idea combines the strongest details. Here, height, colour, and a long curve work together to create a sky-bridge image.
masterclass.passage: The coloured band rose beyond the rooftops, stretched over the wet lane, and appeared to join two far edges of the neighbourhood.
masterclass.prompt: State the main image and give two details that create it.

concept_slots.description: Identifies the band as a bridge-like crossing in the sky.
any_of: makes a bridge above the lane

concept_slots.description: Uses the height or curved stretch as one supporting detail.
Uses the detail about joining two far edges.

independent_check.teaching_block: Read the new scene, then explain the comparison with evidence from its shape and position.
independent_check.passage: From a hill path, Sana saw colours bend over the valley. The two ends seemed to touch fields on opposite sides.
independent_check.prompt: Why could Sana describe the colours as a path between the fields?

concept_slots.description: Uses the bending or path-like shape as evidence.
any_of: formed an arc over the valley

concept_slots.description: Explains that the ends seemed to connect opposite fields.
any_of: seemed to join the two fields
reached from one field to the other

forbidden_phrases: the colours were on the ground

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the comparison method to a different natural image: name what is compared and the feature that supports it.
transfer_check.passage: A break in the clouds let one wide beam of sunlight fall across the dark hills. Dev called it a golden road from the sky.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain why golden road is an effective comparison for the beam of light.

concept_slots.description: Identifies the beam of sunlight as the thing being compared.
Explains that the long bright strip resembles a road or route.
any_of: resembled a road from the sky

forbidden_phrases: the beam was under the hills

levels.title: Unlock words and references
levels.focus: use context to understand key words and track what reference words mean
levels.teaching_goal: Infer the meanings of bow, bridge, and overtop, then connect words such as it, they, and these to the correct ideas.

guided_check.teaching_block: Nearby details can reveal meaning. If one object is higher than another, it overtops the lower object.
guided_check.passage: The festival wheel overtopped every tent, so its highest seats could be seen from outside the fairground.
guided_check.prompt: What does overtopped mean in this sentence?

bridge.teaching_block: A familiar word can have several meanings. The rest of the sentence tells whether bow means a curved shape, a ribbon knot, or an action.
bridge.passage: The acrobat lifted a ribbon into a wide bow above her head, making a smooth arc.
bridge.prompt: Which meaning of bow fits this scene?

masterclass.teaching_block: Reference words avoid repetition. Replace these with the nearest group of nouns that can perform the action in the next clause.
masterclass.passage: Small ferries and fishing boats waited near the jetty. These would cross the inlet after the fog lifted.
masterclass.prompt: What does these refer to, and which clue confirms your answer?

concept_slots.description: Identifies the ferries and fishing boats as the reference.
any_of: the ferries and the fishing boats

concept_slots.description: Uses their ability or plan to cross the inlet as confirmation.
any_of: planned to cross after the fog

independent_check.teaching_block: Use both sentence meaning and reference tracking in this new scene. Explain the word rather than guessing from spelling.
independent_check.passage: Two kites climbed beyond the school roof. They soon overtopped the water tank as well.
independent_check.prompt: What does they refer to, and what does overtopped tell you about their position?

concept_slots.description: Identifies the two kites as the meaning of they.
Explains that the kites rose or flew above the tank.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply both strategies to an unfamiliar market scene: infer a word from position and resolve a pronoun from the action.
transfer_check.passage: A striped canopy overtopped the fruit stalls. It kept the sellers shaded at noon.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain overtopped and identify what it refers to.

concept_slots.description: Explains that the canopy was higher than or above the stalls.
Identifies the striped canopy as the meaning of it.

levels.title: Hear rhyme and contrast
levels.focus: listen for matching end sounds and use opposites to sharpen meaning
levels.teaching_goal: Recognize rhyme by sound, identify opposites from context, and combine both answers in a complete sentence.

guided_check.teaching_block: Rhyming words share an ending sound. Say each choice aloud; spelling alone may not reveal the rhyme.
guided_check.passage: Target word: rain. Listen to train, tree, road, and cloud.

bridge.teaching_block: Opposite words contrast one feature at a time. Curved and straight describe different shapes.
bridge.passage: The ribbon made a curved loop, but the ruler formed a ___ line.

masterclass.teaching_block: Sound and meaning are different tests. Through rhymes with blue, while dim contrasts with bright.
masterclass.passage: Word set: blue, through, dim, bright.
masterclass.prompt: Name the rhyming pair and the opposite pair in one complete sentence.

concept_slots.description: Identifies blue and through as the rhyming pair.
any_of: rhyming pair is blue and through

concept_slots.description: Identifies dim and bright as opposites.
any_of: bright is the opposite of dim
opposite pair is dim and bright

independent_check.teaching_block: Work without choices. Use the target words, then state both findings as a complete sentence.
independent_check.passage: Target rhyme: bright. Word set: night, narrow, dull, bright.
independent_check.prompt: Which word rhymes with bright, and which word is the opposite of dull?

concept_slots.description: Identifies night as the word that rhymes with bright.
Identifies bright as the opposite of dull.
any_of: bright is the opposite of dull

forbidden_phrases: night is the opposite of dull

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the two tests to a fresh set. Listen for sound first, then compare meaning.
transfer_check.passage: Target rhyme: play. Word set: grey, rough, smooth, tall.
transfer_check.prompt: Identify the rhyme for play and the opposite of rough in one complete sentence.

concept_slots.description: Identifies grey as the word that rhymes with play.
Identifies smooth as the opposite of rough.
any_of: smooth is the opposite of rough

forbidden_phrases: grey is the opposite of rough

levels.title: Build and use words
levels.focus: form compound words and distinguish noun, verb, and adjective jobs
levels.teaching_goal: Join meaningful word parts, then use sentence context to explain how a familiar word functions.

guided_check.teaching_block: A compound word combines two smaller words while keeping both ideas. Rain plus bow names a colourful arc seen with rain and light.

bridge.teaching_block: A noun names something; a verb shows an action. The same spelling can do either job, so read the whole sentence.
bridge.passage: Mira used a wide brush to spread blue paint across the chart.
bridge.prompt: What job does brush do in this sentence?

masterclass.teaching_block: Build the compound in its original order, then place it in a sentence that shows its meaning.
masterclass.prompt: Form the compound word and use it in a complete sentence about a room.

concept_slots.description: Forms and uses the compound word sunlight.
Connects sunlight with entering, lighting, or warming a room.

independent_check.teaching_block: Compare two uses of one word. Decide whether each use names a thing or shows an action, and cite the sentence clue.
independent_check.passage: Ravi opened a tin of paint. Later, he will paint a blue arc on the wall.
independent_check.prompt: Explain the two jobs performed by paint.

concept_slots.description: Identifies paint in a tin as a noun naming a material.
any_of: paint in the tin is a noun
names the material in the tin
the first use names a thing

concept_slots.description: Identifies will paint as a verb showing an action.
any_of: the second use is an action

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply compound-building and sentence-writing to a new nature word. Keep the two word parts in the given order.
transfer_check.prompt: Form the compound word and use it in a complete sentence that shows its meaning.

concept_slots.description: Forms and uses the compound word waterfall.
Shows water dropping from a height or over rocks.

levels.title: Trace the colour sequence
levels.focus: read and explain the seven-colour order using VIBGYOR
levels.teaching_goal: Use the VIBGYOR memory aid to locate missing colours, check order, and explain sequence corrections in complete short answers.

guided_check.teaching_block: VIBGYOR stores the standard sequence: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red.
guided_check.passage: V I B G Y O R
guided_check.prompt: Which colour is represented by the first letter?

bridge.teaching_block: Read the sequence from left to right and compare each position with VIBGYOR rather than relying on the colour names alone.
bridge.passage: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, ___, Orange, Red
bridge.prompt: Which colour belongs in the empty fifth position?

masterclass.teaching_block: To repair a sequence, locate the first position that breaks the remembered order and replace only that entry.
masterclass.passage: A chart reads: Violet, Indigo, Green, Blue, Yellow, Orange, Red.
masterclass.prompt: Which two colours are out of order, and how should that part read?

concept_slots.description: Identifies blue and green as the misplaced pair.
any_of: blue and green are out of order
the error is green before blue

concept_slots.description: States that blue must come before green.
any_of: correct order is blue and green

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the sequence in a new craft context and explain the missing position without answer choices.
independent_check.passage: Anu threads beads in this order: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, ___, red.
independent_check.prompt: Name the missing bead colour and explain where it belongs.

concept_slots.description: Identifies orange as the missing colour.
Places orange between yellow and red.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the sequence to initials only. Expand the relevant letters and describe their position clearly.
transfer_check.passage: A light display is labelled V-I-B-G-Y-O-R. The technician asks about the letters on either side of G.
transfer_check.prompt: Which colours come immediately before and after green?

concept_slots.description: States that blue comes immediately before green.
any_of: the colour before green is blue

concept_slots.description: States that yellow comes immediately after green.
any_of: the colour after green is yellow

levels.title: Shape a journey paragraph
levels.focus: plan and write an organized past-tense account of a journey
levels.teaching_goal: Select past-tense verbs, order journey details, and write a clear first-person paragraph in original language.

guided_check.teaching_block: A journey that has already happened needs past-tense verbs such as travelled, reached, noticed, and returned.
guided_check.passage: Last Sunday, we ___ by bus to the lake and returned before sunset.
guided_check.prompt: Which verb completes the past-tense sentence?

bridge.teaching_block: A useful plan includes when and where, who travelled, how the group moved, one memorable event, and a closing feeling.
bridge.passage: Plan A lists only a place. Plan B lists time, destination, companion, transport, one event, and a final feeling.
bridge.prompt: Which plan can support a complete journey paragraph?

masterclass.teaching_block: Order notes as beginning, event, and reflection. Keep verbs in the past so the reader can follow the completed journey.
masterclass.passage: Notes: felt proud at the end / cycled to the old fort with my sister / climbed the final slope slowly.
masterclass.prompt: Summarize the journey in order using at least two past-tense actions and the ending feeling.

concept_slots.description: Begins with cycling to the old fort with the sister.
any_of: cycled to the old fort with my sister
rode with my sister to the old fort
my sister and I cycled to the fort

concept_slots.description: Includes climbing the final slope slowly.
any_of: rode up the final slope slowly

concept_slots.description: Ends with feeling proud.

independent_check.teaching_block: Write an original account with a clear beginning, ordered events, at least three past-tense actions, and a relevant reflection.
independent_check.passage: Think of a real or imagined journey during which the weather changed and you noticed something colourful outdoors.
independent_check.prompt: Write an 80 to 100 word first-person journey paragraph. Include the destination, how and with whom you travelled, at least three past-tense actions, the weather change, and your final feeling.

rubric_criteria.description: Names a destination and explains how and with whom the writer travelled.
Uses at least three clear past-tense actions in a logical order.
Includes a weather change and one specific colourful outdoor detail.
Ends with a relevant feeling or reflection in the writer's own words.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the planning method to diary notes. Turn every note into an ordered past-tense account rather than copying the slash-separated list.
transfer_check.passage: Saturday notes: bicycle ride to the library / cousin came along / sudden drizzle / colour arc above the playground / returned before dark.
transfer_check.prompt: Write a three-sentence diary summary of at least 25 words using all the notes in a sensible order.

concept_slots.description: States that the writer rode a bicycle to the library with a cousin.
any_of: rode my bicycle to the library with my cousin
cycled with my cousin to the library
my cousin and I rode to the library

concept_slots.description: Includes the drizzle and the colour arc above the playground.
any_of: drizzle began and a colour arc appeared
saw a colour arc above the playground after the drizzle
rain fell before colours appeared over the playground
sudden drizzle revealed a colourful arc

concept_slots.description: Ends with returning before dark.
any_of: rode back before it became dark

levels.title: Compare two kinds of bridges
levels.focus: compare a natural rainbow with human-made crossings and support conclusions with evidence
levels.teaching_goal: State an accurate similarity and difference, classify natural and human-made features, and justify the comparison with passage evidence.

guided_check.teaching_block: People construct human-made objects. Natural events form without being assembled by people.
guided_check.passage: Engineers fixed steel beams across the canal so walkers could reach the opposite bank.
guided_check.prompt: How should the steel crossing be classified?

bridge.teaching_block: A strong comparison names one shared feature and one important difference. Both images may look like crossings, but only one is built for travel.
bridge.passage: A stone bridge curved over a stream. Above it, a rainbow curved through the clearing sky.
bridge.prompt: Which statement gives both a similarity and a difference?
options: Both curve over a space, but only the stone bridge carries travellers.
Both are made from stone and steel.
The rainbow carries people while the bridge fades.
The two shapes have nothing in common.
accepted_answers: Both curve over a space, but only the stone bridge carries travellers.
both curve over a space but only the stone bridge carries travellers

masterclass.teaching_block: Use evidence for each side of a comparison: shape can support the similarity, while material, purpose, or permanence can support the difference.
masterclass.passage: Workers built an arched walkway from brick. Later, sunlight and fine spray formed a coloured arc above a fountain.
masterclass.prompt: Compare the walkway and the coloured arc with one similarity and one evidence-based difference.

concept_slots.description: States that both have an arch or curved shape.
Explains that people built the brick walkway while light and spray formed the natural arc.
any_of: coloured arc formed from sunlight and spray
arc formed naturally but the walkway was built
one is brick and the other is light and spray

independent_check.teaching_block: Read the fresh valley scene, then compare purpose and appearance without answer choices.
independent_check.passage: A rope footbridge helped farmers cross a narrow valley. After a shower, a rainbow appeared much higher and faded within minutes.
independent_check.prompt: Give one similarity and one difference between the footbridge and the rainbow, using evidence from the scene.

concept_slots.description: States that both span, cross, or arc over the valley space.
Contrasts the bridge's travel purpose or lasting structure with the high, temporary rainbow.
any_of: footbridge remained after the rainbow faded
bridge is for travel but the rainbow is not

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer comparison and reasoning to a new pair. Organize the answer around a shared shape, different origins, and different duration or purpose.
transfer_check.passage: A greenhouse has a clear arched roof that protects plants throughout the year. One misty morning, a colour arc formed above the garden and disappeared as the air dried.
transfer_check.prompt: In 35 to 55 words, compare the greenhouse roof and the colour arc. Include one accurate similarity, two differences, and a reason the colour arc is natural.
transfer_check.preflight_rule: The response must contain 35 to 55 original English words comparing the greenhouse roof with the temporary natural colour arc.

rubric_criteria.description: States that both the roof and colour arc have a curved or arched shape.
Explains that people built the greenhouse roof while mist, light, or weather formed the colour arc.
Contrasts the lasting protective roof with the temporary arc that disappeared.
Gives a clear reason the colour arc is a natural event.

items.passage: At dusk, a band of colours curved above the football field while puddles still shone near the goalposts.
items.prompt: What appeared above the football field?

items.passage: A brief shower cooled the village. When sunlight returned, a coloured arc appeared above the grain market, and families stopped to admire it.
items.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A rainbow appeared after rain and drew people's attention.
The grain market closed because the village became cold.
Families hurried away before the sunlight returned.
A storm damaged every shop in the grain market.
accepted_answers: A rainbow appeared after rain and drew people's attention.
a rainbow appeared after rain and people admired it

items.passage: Leela left the narrow courtyard and walked to the open terrace when the western sky brightened after rain.
items.prompt: Why did Leela probably move to the open terrace? Use two clues from the passage.

concept_slots.description: Infers that Leela wanted a wider or clearer view of the sky.
any_of: wanted a clear view of the sky
could see more from the terrace
terrace gave her a wider view

concept_slots.description: Uses the brightening western sky after rain as supporting evidence.
any_of: rain had ended and the sky brightened

forbidden_phrases: she wanted to hide from the sky

items.passage: A row of lamps arched over the entrance, forming a smooth curve from one pillar to the other.
items.prompt: What does arched mean in this sentence?

items.passage: Word bank: overtop - to rise higher than something else.
items.prompt: Use overtop in a complete sentence about a kite and a tree.

concept_slots.description: Uses overtop or an inflected form correctly.
Shows that the kite is or becomes higher than the tree.

items.passage: Notes: colours / spread / above the paddy field.
items.prompt: Turn all the notes into one complete sentence.

concept_slots.description: Uses colours as the subject.
Places the colours above the paddy field.
any_of: across the sky above the paddy field

items.passage: The artists colour the paper strips before hanging them across the hall.
items.prompt: What job does colour perform in this sentence?

items.passage: The rain stopped before the school picnic began, and the class could spread its mats on the grass.
items.prompt: In one complete sentence, explain what the class could do after the rain stopped.

concept_slots.description: States that the class could spread or place its mats.
any_of: they could put out the mats

concept_slots.description: States that the mats were spread on the grass.

items.passage: Yesterday, Farhan ___ across the river by ferry and watched clouds gather behind the hills.
items.prompt: Which verb correctly completes the past-tense sentence?

items.passage: A short shower darkened the playground. Soon the sun returned, a pale rainbow appeared, and the children resumed their cricket match.
items.prompt: Summarize the changing scene in one sentence using your own words.

concept_slots.description: Captures the change from a shower to returning sunlight.
any_of: rain stopped and the sun returned
after a short shower the sun came out
playground changed from rainy to sunny

concept_slots.description: Includes the rainbow and the children resuming cricket.
any_of: rainbow appeared and children played cricket
children resumed cricket under a rainbow
pale rainbow appeared before the match continued
cricket restarted when the rainbow appeared

items.passage: Nisha called the rainbow a silent bridge because its long curve seemed to connect the wet orchard with a distant hill.
items.prompt: Why did Nisha use the word bridge? Answer with the visual evidence.

concept_slots.description: Explains that the rainbow looked like a connection or crossing.
Uses the curve between the orchard and hill as evidence.
any_of: curve connected the orchard and hill
stretched from the wet orchard to the hill
long curve reached toward a distant hill
linked the orchard with the hill

items.passage: A blue kite makes a curved path only while the wind carries it. A rainbow forms a coloured curve after rain and remains in one part of the sky for a short time.
items.prompt: In 25 to 45 words, compare the kite's path and the rainbow. Name both, give one similarity, and give one accurate difference.
items.preflight_rule: The response must contain 25 to 45 original English words comparing the moving kite path with the short-lived rainbow.

rubric_criteria.description: Names both the kite or kite path and the rainbow.
States that both make a curved shape or path in the sky.
Explains that the wind moves the kite while the rainbow is a coloured weather image that briefly stays in one area.

items.passage: Three cyclists paused beside the canal and pointed toward a faint arc beyond the sugarcane fields.
items.prompt: What did the cyclists point toward?

items.passage: The science club sprayed a fine mist beside a sunny window. Tiny colours appeared in the mist, helping the group see how light and water can create a rainbow effect.
items.prompt: Which sentence states the main idea?
options: The club used sunlight and mist to observe a rainbow effect.
The club washed every window before science class.
The students avoided using water during the activity.
The mist blocked all light from entering the room.
accepted_answers: The club used sunlight and mist to observe a rainbow effect.
sunlight and mist helped the club observe rainbow colours

items.passage: Aarav packed the painted banner indoors when dark clouds covered the sun, but he carried it outside again as soon as a bright patch opened in the sky.
items.prompt: Why did Aarav carry the banner outside again?
options: The weather looked brighter and safer for displaying it.
He wanted the dark clouds to soak the banner.
The room had become too sunny for the banner.
He had forgotten that the banner was painted.
accepted_answers: The weather looked brighter and safer for displaying it.
the sky brightened so he could display it outside

items.passage: The new flyover spanned the railway tracks, reaching from the bus depot to the hospital road.
items.prompt: What does spanned mean here?

items.passage: Word bank: arc - a curved line or shape.
items.prompt: Use arc in a complete sentence about water from a fountain.

concept_slots.description: Uses the word arc to name a curved shape.
Connects the arc to water moving from or above a fountain.

items.passage: Notes: the orange scarf / fluttered / beside the open window.
items.prompt: Write one complete sentence using every note.

concept_slots.description: Uses the orange scarf as subject with the action fluttered.
Places the scarf beside the open window.

forbidden_phrases: scarf was behind a closed door

items.passage: A narrow bridge connected the two garden paths.
items.prompt: What job does bridge perform in this sentence?

items.passage: A colour chart reads violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red.
items.prompt: In one sentence, state which colour comes after green and before orange.

concept_slots.description: Identifies yellow as the colour in the requested position.
any_of: yellow is between green and orange

concept_slots.description: Places yellow after green and before orange.

forbidden_phrases: blue is between green and orange

items.passage: During our trip last month, we ___ the hill station before noon and explored the market after lunch.
items.prompt: Which past-tense verb completes the sentence?

items.passage: Mehul and his grandmother rode a train through heavy rain. Near the final station, sunlight broke through, colours appeared over the farms, and both travellers smiled.
items.prompt: Summarize the journey and its final change in one sentence using your own words.

concept_slots.description: Includes Mehul and his grandmother travelling by train through rain.
any_of: Mehul and his grandmother travelled by train through rain
they rode a train in heavy rain
train journey began in heavy rain
grandmother and Mehul travelled through rain

concept_slots.description: Captures the later sunlight, colours, and positive reaction.
any_of: sunlight and colours made them smile
colours appeared over farms when the sun returned

forbidden_phrases: sunlight came before the rain began

items.passage: Carpenters built a wooden arch for the school stage. That evening, a rainbow formed above the playground after a shower.
items.prompt: Why is the wooden arch human-made while the rainbow is natural?

concept_slots.description: Explains that carpenters or people constructed the wooden arch.
Explains that the rainbow formed through weather, light, or rain without people building it.
any_of: light and rain made the rainbow
people did not build the rainbow

items.passage: A concrete flyover carries buses above a busy road every day. A rainbow may arch above the same road after rain, but it cannot carry traffic and soon fades.
items.prompt: In 30 to 50 words, compare the flyover and rainbow. Name both, give one visual similarity, and give two accurate differences.
items.preflight_rule: The response must contain 30 to 50 original English words comparing the lasting traffic flyover with the temporary natural rainbow.

rubric_criteria.description: Names both the concrete flyover and the rainbow.
States that both arch, curve, or stretch above the road.
Explains that the flyover carries traffic while the rainbow cannot.
Contrasts the lasting built flyover with the temporary natural rainbow.
